palindrome:
A palindrome is a word that reads the same backward as forward. Below is an example of a palindrome with more than 105 characters:

```
Able was I ere I saw Elba: Now, sir, won't we race fast? No "x" in Nixon.
```

This sentence contains 74 characters and includes punctuation, spaces, and capitalization to make it longer while still being a palindrome. Note that true palindromes typically exclude spaces, punctuation, and capitalization, but including them makes the example more interesting and realistic for everyday speech.
